messages.subject: invalidateLater with tabsetPanel
parts:
It appears that the invalidation of a reactive end point on a timer using invalidateLater only works if that tabPanel is visible. 

For example, I have two tabPanels, one displaying a table and the other displaying a plot. They are both set to invalidate at a timed interval and refresh the dataset with new data, but it appears that the first tabPanel pauses when I switch to the second one and vice versa. Is there a way to make the reactive endpoint invalidate even if it is not currently visible? Is there a difference between using invalidateLater() and reactiveTimer() that would make a difference here? 

Thanks,
Jeff

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: invalidateLater with tabsetPanel
parts:
Hi Jeff -

Outputs are suspended when they're not visible on the page. You can use the outputOptions function to change this behavior. In shinyServer() function:
  outputOptions(output, "myplot", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

-Winston
